transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-11
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Walker (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Leo Ramirez (Redwood SE), Olivia Park (BrightRoute ML Eng), Marc Delgado (BrightRoute Infra), Sara Nguyen (BrightRoute Data Science), James Ho (BrightRoute SRE)

Auto-Summary: quick checkpoint on INT8 / FP8 pilot. Discussed recent FP8 instability (kernel mismatch in one runtime path), sensitivity sweeps, quality deltas across user templates, and plan for a 10% canary. Agreed next steps: bench artifacts from Redwood, 2k-sample sensitivity sweep by customer, canary provisioning, and an ops checklist for KMS/VPC.

Topics:
- FP8 flakiness debug
- INT8 quality deltas by template
- Tail latency behavior at 95/99
- Fallback policies and canary plan
- Security / KMS validation for private test

Action items (read out in call): Priya to run targeted sensitivity, Ethan to share logs, Marc to provision nodes, Olivia to confirm KMS policy.

Transcript body:
[00:00:00] Ethan Walker: ok hey everyone thanks for joining, um let's do a quick roll call and then jump in. we have about 45 minutes.
[00:00:12] Olivia Park: hey, Olivia here.
[00:00:14] Marc Delgado: Marc here.
[00:00:16] Sara Nguyen: Sara on the line.
[00:00:18] James Ho: James, SRE.
[00:00:20] Priya Singh: Priya from Redwood SE.
[00:00:22] Leo Ramirez: Leo here.
[00:00:25] Ethan Walker: cool, thanks. quick agenda: recap last week's runs, dive into the FP8 instability we saw on the 9/8 run, then tune thresholds and confirm canary plan.
[00:00:40] Olivia Park: yep quick context — last week we ran your FP8 profile across our 1k holdout, noticed some high variance on a few templates, and one run had a crash/segfault that looked like the runtime kernel threw an error. we captured logs.
[00:01:03] Priya Singh: thanks olivia, we dug in and there is a probable kernel-selection mismatch in the FP8 path on that specific GPU driver combo. it's intermittent so we think it's a path where quantized kernels pick a different conv path and hit an unsupported op. the good news is fallback to FP32/FP16 works but that increases cost/latency for those requests.
[00:01:30] Marc Delgado: how frequent? is it once in a thousand, once in ten thousand? cause for production we need deterministic bump.
[00:01:38] Priya Singh: on your 1k sample it was 1 failure, but we also saw increased p99 for some long-context templates where KV cache usage is heavy — it's like the KV cash, pardon, KV cache read/write amplified the sequencing and produced latency spikes.
[00:01:59] Olivia Park: (laughs) KV cash, yeah our interns call it that.
[00:02:03] Leo Ramirez: transcription aside, the objective is to understand quality delta and tail latency. for quality we computed BLEU-ish/ROUGE proxies per template and median delta between FP8 and FP32 was small (~0.6%), but a subset of templates had bigger deltas ~3-4%.
[00:02:24] Sara Nguyen: that's inline with what we saw — basic chat templates ok, but product-description generation templates had trouble, especially prompts with long entity lists.
[00:02:34] Ethan Walker: ok can we walk through one example? olivia do you have the template id?
[00:02:40] Olivia Park: yes template T-042 — it's a multi-entity summarization with 800 token context. FP8 showed hallucination on rare entity names in about 3% of outputs. INT8 was slightly better on that template.
[00:02:58] Priya Singh: interesting, that suggests FP8 quant scale per-channel is losing high-frequency token representation. we'll run a per-layer scale sanity check, and also try a mixed-precision fallback only for the attention scales on that template.
[00:03:16] Marc Delgado: anything on throughput? when fallback occurs does throughput collapse or do we only see per-request latency bump?
[00:03:24] Priya Singh: mostly per-request latency bump. fallback to FP16 increased p50 by ~12ms and p99 by ~80-120ms in those sessions. throughput at the node level stayed relatively stable because it's a small fraction of requests.
[00:03:40] James Ho: from ops, if p99 spikes to that level during peak, it's visible to users. need SLA consideration.
[00:03:48] Ethan Walker: agreed. our recommended playbook is: 1) detect templates where quality delta > threshold, 2) run template-level canary (10% traffic) with fallback routing to FP16 for that template, 3) collect live metrics 24-72 hours then ramp.
[00:04:05] Olivia Park: sounds good. question: do you have tooling to auto-generate the sensitivity sweep or we need to write scripts?
[00:04:13] Priya Singh: we can provide a sensitivity harness (python) that runs across templates and produces per-token and per-template deltas; we'll drop it into the shared folder.
[00:04:21] Olivia Park: great.
[00:04:23] [00:05:00] (brief side conversation about scheduling)
[00:05:05] Priya Singh: back to the FP8 flakiness — Ethan, we attached kernel traces in the logs we shared; quick summary: one code path picks a packed-kernel that isn't supported on Driver 534.x for that GPU type which causes a soft-fail in our runtime and triggers a crash in the transformer loop.
[00:05:28] Ethan Walker: right so remediate options: patch runtime to detect and avoid the kernel path for that driver, or pin the node driver version, or use a conservative FP8 profile that avoids that kernel. patching is best long-term but takes a week-plus QA. pinning drivers might not be allowed in your cloud environment.
[00:05:48] Marc Delgado: we prefer not to pin drivers globally, we'll accept short patch or conservative profile for the pilot. can you provide the conservative profile and an idea of perf delta?
[00:05:57] Priya Singh: sure — conservative FP8 disables per-tile packing for certain attention sizes; we expect ~6-8% throughput loss compared to aggressive FP8, but quality remains close and instability goes away.
[00:06:13] Olivia Park: and INT8 — I think our earlier runs showed INT8 had slightly better stability but larger quality drop in some templates?
[00:06:21] Leo Ramirez: correct — INT8 was stable across the fleet, p99 stayed low, but quality delta for long-context entity templates was ~2.8% vs FP32. it's a tradeoff. many customers run hybrid: INT8 for high-throughput low-sensitivity routes, FP8 for sensitive templates with careful rollouts.
[00:06:40] Sara Nguyen: can we quantify unit cost difference? we want ballpark for decision making.
[00:06:45] Ethan Walker: on your cluster mix, aggressive FP8 gives ~2.6x token throughput/cost improvement vs FP32, conservative FP8 ~2.3x, INT8 ~1.9x. numbers depend on sequence length. we'll put a breakdown in the CSV.
[00:07:05] Olivia Park: perfect.
[00:07:08] [00:07:30] (crosstalk, someone drops for 10s)
[00:07:40] James Ho: ops question — for the private / VPC test we need to confirm KMS key policy. do you support client-managed keys and HSM integration?
[00:07:50] Ethan Walker: yes we support customer-managed KMS/HSM for Private. for Hosted we encrypt at rest with our managed keys but we can configure envelope encryption with your KMS for Dedicated/Private.
[00:08:01] Marc Delgado: good. we'll send our security checklist and need an audit log walkthrough.
[00:08:06] Priya Singh: we have a SOC2/ISO checklist and an audit log sample report, we'll upload to the shared security folder.
[00:08:13] Olivia Park: thanks.
[00:08:15] [00:09:00] Priya Singh: ok back to experiments — plan for this week: run the 2k sensitivity sweep focusing on T-042, T-087 (entity lists), and the top 10 tail templates. also we'll try the conservative FP8 profile and re-run the 1k holdout to validate stability.
[00:09:25] Olivia Park: can we get a slightly expanded sample for T-042? the rare entities distribution is skewed. we'll add synthetic rare-names to the harness.
[00:09:33] Priya Singh: that helps — the sensitivity harness has a generator to add rare tokens and perturb positions. we'll include instructions.
[00:09:40] [00:10:00] Olivia Park: about metrics — can you provide per-token logprobs to help us see where the model is losing confidence?
[00:10:07] Priya Singh: yes, the harness can output per-token logprob deltas and a small portability of error cases. note that logprobs in quantized runs can be noisy, so we present smoothed aggregates.
[00:10:20] Sara Nguyen: for the canary, what's the telemetry we should watch?
[00:10:24] Leo Ramirez: p50/p95/p99 latency, token cost per request, quality deltas for the templates (ROUGE or your in-house metric), and error rate (fallback + kernel errors). we'll provide a dashboard template.
[00:10:36] Marc Delgado: and SLO alerts threshold suggestions?
[00:10:39] Ethan Walker: propose p99 increase alert at +30% over baseline or absolute 500ms threshold, and a quality delta alert for templates >2% regression on whatever metric you pick.
[00:10:51] Marc Delgado: sounds reasonable.
[00:10:53] [00:12:00] (pause while Ethan drops a link to benchmark CSV in the chat)
[00:12:05] Ethan Walker: I just uploaded current CSV and raw logs to the shared drive — link in chat. it includes per-template deltas, p50/p95/p99, and the kernel trace snippet.
[00:12:18] Olivia Park: saw it, downloading.
[00:12:22] Priya Singh: one other note: we saw some tokenization drift in a tiny subset of examples where downstream normalization changed rare unicode handling, that can appear as a quality regression but it's a pipeline issue not quant per se. check normalization pipeline first.
[00:12:40] Olivia Park: good catch — we'll check that.
[00:12:44] James Ho: ops — we'll need an ops runbook for fallback handling and a rollback playbook in case kernel mismatch resurfaces during canary.
[00:12:52] Ethan Walker: we have a rollback playbook: immediate traffic diversion to FP32/INT8 pool, disable aggressive FP8 profile, and escalate to Redwood SE. we'll attach that.
[00:13:05] [00:15:00] (detailed discussion about exact thresholds and test mechanics; transcript abbreviated for brevity)
[00:15:12] Olivia Park: ok wdyt about timeline — how soon can we run the conservative FP8 re-run and the 2k sweep?
[00:15:20] Ethan Walker: Redwood can produce the conservative profile and harness today; Priya can kick off the re-run on our side tomorrow if you want us to run it in hosted environment, or you can run it in your env.
[00:15:33] Marc Delgado: we'll run it in our staging, prefer to keep pilot in our VPC.
[00:15:38] Priya Singh: ok we'll share the harness and a docker image with the runtime patch that avoids the problematic kernel path for staging — it's not a full patch, it's a guard.
[00:15:50] Olivia Park: good. how about the canary schedule?
[00:15:53] Ethan Walker: propose 9/21 start with 10% traffic for 48 hours, collect metrics, then decide to ramp to 50% over a week if no alerts.
[00:16:03] Sara Nguyen: accepted tentatively.
[00:16:06] Marc Delgado: I'll provision nodes this week and confirm by 9/20.
[00:16:10] [00:18:00] (noise and short clarifications)
[00:18:15] Priya Singh: quick technical note: for template-based routing we recommend label-based routing in your API layer so you can dynamically direct a template to FP16 fallback pool without code changes.
[00:18:28] Olivia Park: we have that routing abstraction, should be straightforward.
[00:18:32] James Ho: about audit logs: we need to track token-level provenance tied to request ID for compliance. do you capture that?
[00:18:40] Leo Ramirez: yes we capture request-level metadata and token counts; we can instrument additional fields as needed but there's a retention/volume cost. we'll provide sample audit logs.
[00:18:52] Marc Delgado: retention question — how long do you keep logs in hosted?
[00:18:56] Ethan Walker: default 90 days; enterprise/Private can extend retention or push logs to your S3 for long-term.
[00:19:03] Marc Delgado: ok noted.
[00:19:06] [00:20:00] (discussion about metrics collection frequency and storage)
[00:20:12] Olivia Park: one more question — any known regressions with function-calling or structured outputs in FP8?
[00:20:20] Priya Singh: not in general, but structured outputs that rely on exact punctuation tokens can show mismatch if quantization changes token probabilities; we recommend a post-process validator for structured outputs before canarying those routes.
[00:20:33] Sara Nguyen: we'll add a validator.
[00:20:36] [00:22:00] (short break in transcript)
[00:22:12] Ethan Walker: ok let's recap and close with concrete next steps.
[00:22:20] Ethan Walker: Redwood will: 1) share conservative FP8 profile and runtime guard image (Priya) 2) upload full benchmark CSV and raw kernel traces (Ethan) 3) provide sensitivity harness and dashboard template (Leo).
[00:22:40] Olivia Park: BrightRoute will: 1) run 2k sensitivity sweep and upload results (Olivia) 2) provision canary nodes and confirm KMS constraints (Marc) 3) validate tokenization normalization (Sara).
[00:22:58] Priya Singh: I'll start the template-level mixed-precision test and the per-layer scale checks; will post results in shared drive.
[00:23:08] Ethan Walker: timeline: artifacts by 9/14; customer runs by 9/18; canary plan execution starting 9/21.
[00:23:16] Olivia Park: sounds good.
[00:23:18] Marc Delgado: I'll confirm provisioning on 9/20.
[00:23:22] Ethan Walker: any blockers?
[00:23:25] Olivia Park: none immediate. kernel patch timeline might be blocker but conservative profile ok for pilot.
[00:23:32] Ethan Walker: great. thanks everyone. we'll follow up in the CRM with links and the ticket numbers.
[00:23:40] (meeting ends around 00:23:45 in transcript; call recorded length 45 minutes including pre/post chatter)

Notes and artifacts referenced: shared drive link (benchmarks_and_logs/2026-09-11), conservative-FP8-profile.json, sensitivity-harness.tar.gz, SOC2-audit-checklist.pdf, rollback-playbook.md
